title: Broad train/holdout opponent-domain feasibility
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: A frozen set of six training opponents and three gradient-untouched holdout opponents drawn from distinct learned lineages can be loaded under explicit physical-v6 observation contracts and exhibits enough reachable-state action disagreement to support a broader multi-seed geometric MGDA curve.
material_change: Freeze a preregistered nine-policy identity manifest; generate 4,096 outcome-blind legal physical-v6 states; auto-resolve each checkpoint observation contract; query every policy without changing weights; measure physical-action signatures, pairwise greedy disagreement, probability divergence, contract breadth, and strict train/holdout SHA disjointness. No training or external evaluation hands.
baseline: Current MGDA used only Standard10, Slumbot-free, and CFR96 as both gradient groups and evaluation anchors; its seed1 20k external confirmation was -47.525 bb/100 CI[-67.1694,-27.8806].
notes: Admission requires all nine frozen identities unique and loadable, no train/holdout overlap, 4,096 valid state queries per policy, minimum train-pair disagreement 2%, and each holdout at least 1% greedy-disagreement from its nearest training identity. Passing only authorizes trainer redesign and a 3x65,536 first curve; it does not claim poker-strength improvement.

Preregistered first set failed only the unchanged 2% train-pair diversity gate: physical_1m was 0.8301% different from Standard10. Recovery removes physical_1m, promotes the already-preregistered diverse_league5 identity to training, and replaces that holdout with frozen fictitious_response_phase2. Thresholds, state corpus seed/count, all other identities, and train/holdout separation requirements remain unchanged; attempt01 is preserved.

result.summary: A strict recovery set established six frozen training policies and three SHA-disjoint holdouts across legacy-v4 and native-v6 contracts. All nine SHA256 identities and 4,096-state greedy signatures were unique; 36,864 physical-action queries were valid. Minimum train-pair disagreement was 2.5879% and minimum holdout-to-nearest-train disagreement was 34.7656%. The first set's failed 0.8301% redundant physical1m/Standard10 pair remains preserved in attempt01; 246 tests passed.
result.conclusion: A materially broader and gradient-untouched opponent protocol is feasible with existing frozen learned policies. Replacing a demonstrably redundant Standard10-like training identity, without relaxing gates, produced a domain set suitable for a multi-seed geometric training curve. This establishes experimental design feasibility only, not improved poker strength.
result.next_step: Generalize the MGDA fresh-curve trainer from three legacy-only opponents to six mixed-contract training policies plus three evaluation-only holdouts, add restart-safe per-seed checkpoint/accounting, and run a 3-seed 65,536-hand first dose with source-preservation and untouched holdout evaluation.
